items.title: Anwar: University students, institutions among 2027 Budget priorities
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: University students and higher education institutions will be among the key priorities in the 2027 Budget, which is currently being finalised, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. "God willing, university students and universities will certainly also be included in (the Budget). Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, his deputy Adam Adli Abd Halim, and Higher Education Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Aminuddin Hassim.

items.title: F&B operators encouraged to explore more cuts of Japanese Wagyu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian food and beverage (F&B) operators are encouraged to explore a wider range of Japanese Wagyu cuts in their dishes to make the premium beef more accessible to consumers. However, he said growing awareness of Japanese Wagyu among Malaysian consumers presented an opportunity to introduce new ways of enjoying the beef. The seminar was organised by Jetro Kuala Lumpur together with halal-certified Japanese Wagyu supplier Zenrich Allied Sdn Bhd (Zenrich Wagyu) and Kurohana Wagyu Export Promotion Consortium to expand the use of Japanese Wagyu in the food sector.

items.title: #NSTviral: Malaysian cooking oil, sugar spotted for sale in Narathiwat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian packet cooking oil and sugar have been spotted for sale at a market in Narathiwat, Thailand, raising questions over how the controlled goods ended up across the border. The discovery was shared on Threads by user Hafeezboh, who claimed to have spotted Malaysian-made packet cooking oil and sugar while visiting a market in Narathiwat. Meanwhile, Keiko_13r claimed that Malaysian-made packet cooking oil had been spotted not only in southern Thailand but as far as the Philippines.

items.title: Johan Setia, Nilai record unhealthy air quality
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10pm, with Johan Setia in Selangor recording the highest reading at 137. The Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System showed Nilai in Negri Sembilan recorded the second-highest reading at 131. A total of 60 other areas recorded moderate air quality, with API readings between 51 and 100, while six areas recorded good air quality, with readings between 0 and 50, out of 68 monitoring stations nationwide.

items.title: Anwar urges Gen Z to reject wrongdoing, serve the people
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged Gen Z Malaysians to develop greater awareness and determination to serve the people and reject wrongdoing. He said academic achievement alone was not enough, citing scandals involving 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB), Felda and Tabung Haji as examples of how education did not necessarily guarantee integrity or good character. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir was present.

items.title: Anwar clears schedule to focus on 2027 Budget
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has cleared his schedule and cancelled several programmes this week to focus on finalising the 2027 Budget. Anwar, however, said he made an exception for the National Student Icon Award 2026, as he considered the programme which involves student leaders important. Anwar said the government needs to take into account a wide range of demands and needs across sectors, ministries and states in preparing the budget.

items.title: Five detained after RM1mil food, alcohol seizure in Subang Jaya
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Five people, including four Myanmar nationals, were detained after food and alcoholic beverage products worth more than RM1 million were seized in a raid in Subang Jaya. Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence Investigation (WCB/PSK) commander of the Federal Internal Security and Public Order Department Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the five were detained during Op Taring Alpha 5 at 11.30am. Mohd Zaki said the total value of the seizure was estimated at RM1,022,635.20.

items.title: Selangor extends RM30 public transport subsidy to KTM Komuter
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor state government has expanded its RM30 public transport subsidy to KTM Komuter services, effective immediately. State Investment, Trade and Mobility Committee chairman Ng Sze Han said the expansion would enable more users to benefit from the subsidy, which initially covered Rapid KL On-Demand and Kumpool services. Applicants must be registered voters in Selangor.

items.title: 15-year-old boy drowns in Klang lake
items.summary: Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 6.21pm. He said seven firefighters and a fire engine from the Andalas Fire and Rescue Station were sent to the scene, with the search assisted by the Shah Alam Water Rescue Team. "The victim's body was found by the Water Rescue Team at 8.21pm," he said in a statement.

items.title: Terberg drives Malaysia-made tractors into global ports
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Terberg Tractors Malaysia Sdn Bhd has shipped more than 8,000 terminal tractors made in Johor to ports and logistics hubs in over 50 countries. This has turned Terberg Tractors into a significant export base for the Dutch industrial vehicle maker Royal Terberg Group BV Terberg Tractors is a 50:50 joint venture between Sime Darby Bhd's unit Sime Darby Industrial Sdn Bhd and Royal Terberg. Terberg Tractors is also expanding into electric terminal tractors as global ports move towards lower-emission operations.

items.title: 408 MCBA officers start on-site RTS Link training
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A total of 408 pioneer Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officers have begun on-site training ahead of their deployment to the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link entry point. Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link Entry Point Commander Khairul Nizam Hashim said the New Officer Onboarding Programme held today was a continuation of basic training to strengthen their readiness before they are assigned to the field. He said the officers comprised 39 Assistant Border Superintendents and 369 Border Superintendent Assistants.

items.title: ECRL cables stolen three days in a row ahead of operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The public should to stay away from the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) alignment following a series of cable theft and cable-cutting incidents in Selangor that could pose serious safety risks and disrupt ongoing testing and commissioning works. It said the ECRL alignment is an active testing area and is not open to the public, while railway systems, equipment, and cables along the alignment are either powered or undergoing live testing. The company said cable theft and damage to railway infrastructure could also disrupt ongoing testing and commissioning works, as affected equipment would need to be inspected, repaired or replaced before testing could resume.

items.title: Woman trapped in SUV for 30 minutes after trailer crash
items.summary: HULU SELANGOR: A woman was trapped in an SUV for nearly 30 minutes after it was involved in a collision with a trailer on the North-South Expressway. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received a call at 5.34pm and firefighters arrived at the scene 16 minutes later. Upon arrival, we found the woman trapped in the SUV.

items.title: Pregnant motorcyclist loses baby in crash with SUV
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: A motorcyclist who was nine months pregnant lost her unborn baby in a two-vehicle crash at Km4.3 of Jalan Kota Tinggi-Kluang. Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received information about the crash involving the 35-year-old woman, who was riding a SYM motorcycle, and a Nissan X-Trail SUV driven by a 61-year-old man, at 1.55pm. Yusof said the woman was receiving treatment at the hospital, while the SUV driver was uninjured.

items.title: Court overturns acquittal, health officer ordered to enter defence on unnatural sex charges
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today overturned a High Court decision acquitting a health officer of seven charges of having unnatural sex with a woman and ordered him to enter his defence. "The High Court's order upholding the decision of the Sessions Court is set aside. The decision was subsequently upheld by the Kota Baru High Court.

items.title: Democratic wave hitting Republican states hardest, scrambling Senate strategy
items.summary: KENTUCKY Democrats say they have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to flip a US Senate seat in a Republican stronghold. Kentucky is one of several states that President Donald Trump won by double digits in 2024 where Republicans are significantly trailing the president's performance, an indication that Democrats have expanded their pathway to a majority in November's midterm elections. To win the Senate, Democrats must defend two seats in states Trump carried and win four Republican-held seats, including at least two in states Trump won by double digits.

items.title: Anwar: Govt to strengthen governance, curb leakages and abuse of power
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will continue to strengthen public service governance and integrity to curb leakages of public funds and abuse of power, particularly involving Federal Statutory Bodies, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the meeting also agreed to conduct a legal study to formulate the policy and governance direction for a proposed Charities Bill to regulate trust entities and public funding. Anwar said the Madani government would continue to strengthen public service integrity and close avenues for leakages and abuse of power.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - October 1, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: 'Don't become like Selayang' MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain says KLIA must not become a hub for syndicates smuggling drugs, gold and other contraband. Saravanan questions MACC Former Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan has questioned MACC's explanation for his 12-year-old son's presence at its headquarters. Mahathir visits grave Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad visited the grave of his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, at Pusara Negara this morning.

items.title: Hengyuan brings back former CEO Ranta
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd has reappointed former chief executive officer (CEO) Erkki Tapio Ranta to lead the oil refiner effective today. Ranta, 62, replaces Yin LuJiang, 55, who has stepped down as CEO after nearly three years in the role. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Hengyuan said Ranta joined Hengyuan International Sdn Bhd as a senior officer in November 2019 before becoming CEO in March 2020.

items.title: Company manager remanded over alleged RM200m tax reduction fraud
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has remanded a company manager from a financial and corporate services agency for three days. Magistrate Illya Syaheedah Mohd Razif issued the remand order which is in force until Oct 3 following an application by the MACC at the Putrajaya magistrate's court The suspect was arrested around 7pm yesterday when he appeared to provide his statement at the MACC headquarters. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrest and said the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: IOI Properties snaps up Shenton House for RM696mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IOI Properties Group Bhd is taking full ownership of Shenton House in Singapore through the acquisition of its owner, Shenton 101 Pte Ltd, for RM696.43 million. IOI Properties said its unit Boulevard View Pte Ltd will buy 100 per cent of Shenton 101 from group chief executive officer and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng. Shenton House is also within walking distance of IOI Properties' IOI Central Boulevard Towers and Asia Square Tower 2.

items.title: Anwar, Bahrain Crown Prince discuss F1 preparations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim took time during his visit to the Sepang International Circuit today to speak by phone with Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa. In a Facebook post, Anwar said they spoke on preparations for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix race, with the two countries working closely to ensure the event runs smoothly and welcoming fans and visitors from around the world. He also expressed appreciation for the close cooperation between Malaysia and Bahrain in hosting the event.

items.title: Nepal rescuers recover eight bodies after Himalayan avalanche
items.summary: KATHMANDU: Rescuers recovered eight more bodies on Thursday from the area of a Himalayan avalanche that buried 16 expedition workers, in one of the worst mountain disasters in recent years. "The team have found eight bodies today," said Tul Singh Gurung, president of the Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, taking the total to 15, with one person still missing. Nepal's worst mountaineering disasters in recent years occurred in 2014, when an avalanche killed 16 people on Everest, and in 2015, when an earthquake killed 18 people, also on Everest.

items.title: MACC remands brothers with ‘Datuk Seri’, ‘Datuk Wira’ titles over alleged RM10m investment abuse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Two corporate figures, who are brothers, have been remanded for five days over an alleged abuse of position involving an investment of about RM10 million. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) obtained the remand order, effective today until October 5, from Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court this morning. The MACC also seized 15 luxury cars, 12 high-powered motorcycles, five luxury watches, three bracelets and about RM30,000 in cash.

items.title: F1 Bahrain GP: Vehicles must pass five checks before entering Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Vehicles heading to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix tomorrow will have to pass through five designated screening points before being allowed into the circuit grounds. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the checks would cover tickets, vehicle passes and access stickers. "To ensure orderly access control, all vehicles heading to SIC are required to undergo screening at five main locations.

items.title: Smouldering bins, halted trams as French pupils protest
items.summary: PARIS: A high school entrance hall caught fire in one French city and teenage protesters blocked trams in another on Thursday, as secondary pupils upped their strike over what they denounce as poor learning conditions. Some 340 demonstrations were underway in front of high schools mid-morning, with more than 160 establishments shut down as a result, police said. University students joined in on Thursday, blocking physical access to around 30 campuses, including in Paris and the southern city of Marseille, a student union said.

items.title: Hextar Capital secures RM60mil road contract in Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hextar Capital Bhd's subsidiary Legacy Core Sdn Bhd has secured a RM60 million road upgrading subcontract in Sibu, Sarawak. The company said in a Bursa Malaysia filing today that Legacy Core received the contract from the main contractor, Doland (M) Sdn Bhd, for the Jalan Oya project. Legacy Core will undertake road works, drainage and services relocation for the project.

items.title: Euro slides to 17-month low, hit by rates and inflation mix
items.summary: The European currency fell below US$1.13 for the first time since May 2025 against the dollar, which has been in ascendance for the past couple of months, thanks in part to the largest quarterly rise in Treasury yields since 1994. The euro was last down 0.35 per cent at US$1.1291. It declined nearly 2.5 per cent in September, its largest monthly decline since July 2025.

items.title: F1 menu at Sepang features local favourites, draws price praise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix menu at Sepang will feature local favourites including nasi lemak, ayam gepuk and Indomee, with drinks from RM9. The menu has drawn largely positive reactions from users on Threads, with many describing the prices as reasonable for an international sporting event. RM35 for the F1 event is considered okay," user syaffiq7474 wrote.

items.title: Federal Court sets five-day hearing for Petronas, Sarawak oil and gas petitions beginning Jan 25
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court has set five days from Jan 25 next year to hear petitions filed by Petroliam National Bhd (Petronas) and the Sarawak government challenging the state and federal laws governing oil and gas matters. However, she left it to the Federal Court panel hearing the petitions to decide whether to first hear the Sarawak government's preliminary issue on the validity of the Sarawak (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954 (OIC), which concerns the boundaries of Sarawak's territorial waters. However, the state government maintains that its petition should be heard first.

items.title: Johor rolls out additional RM30m after flash floods hit state capital
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 1 — The Johor government will provide an additional allocation of RM30 million next year to fund four urgent measures to address flash flooding in the state capital. Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the allocation aims to fast-track the implementation of short- and medium-term measures to tackle flash floods. Also present were Johor Bahru Mayor Datuk Mohd Haffiz Ahmad and Perling assemblyman P. Pannir Selvam.

items.title: Ajiya to dispose Puchong property for RM58mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ajiya Bhd's subsidiary, Ajiya Safety Glass Sdn Bhd (ASG) has inked a sale and purchase Agreement (SPA) with Esprit Care Sdn Bhd (ECSB) to dispose of a freehold industrial land in Puchong, Selangor for RM58 million. Ajiya said the disposal consideration was arrived at on a willing buyer-willing seller basis, taking into consideration the property's indicative market value of RM40 million, namely RM27 million for the land and RM13 million for the building, as assessed by CBRE WTW Valuation and Advisory Sdn Bhd. It said the proposed disposal is expected to result in an estimated gross gain of RM25.44 million, after taking into account the reversal of deferred tax liability of RM4.47 million.

items.title: Johor government to enhance ‘Smart City’ technology for early extreme weather warnings
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 1 — The Johor government will enhance its ‘Smart City’ technology to enable city residents to receive early flood warnings during extreme heavy rain that poses a risk of flash floods. State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the early flood warning alerts or notifications would be sent directly to mobile phones via a smart application. Mohd Jafni explained that two flood warning sirens were operational during yesterday’s flash flood incident, with each sounding three times.

items.title: Bidor petrol station shooting: Police record nine statements, hunt three suspects
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 1 — Perak police have recorded statements from nine people, including the victim, in their investigation into the shooting of a businessman at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral last Tuesday. Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those whose statements were recorded included three family members who were in the victim’s vehicle, two people in a vehicle near the scene and employees of the petrol station. He said the victim is now in stable condition after receiving treatment and undergoing surgery at Seri Botani Hospital, while police are investigating from various angles, including identifying the motive, which has yet to be established.

items.title: Petronas-Sarawak oil and gas dispute heads to Federal Court for five-day hearing from Jan 25
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Federal Court has set five days from January 25 next year to hear petitions filed by Petroliam National Bhd (Petronas) and the Sarawak Government challenging the state and federal laws governing oil and gas matters. However, she left it to the Federal Court panel hearing the petitions to decide whether to first hear the Sarawak Government’s preliminary issue on the validity of the Sarawak (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954 (OIC), which concerns the boundaries of Sarawak’s territorial waters. However, the state government maintains that its petition should be heard first.

items.title: Don't abuse your power, deputy IGP tells police
items.summary: Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid said leadership was not a privilege to be used for personal gain but a major trust that must be discharged responsibly. “Therefore, I urge that every decision made must be based on integrity, accountability and a sense of fairness,” he said at the handover ceremony for the Sarawak acting police commissioner and acting chairman of the Sarawak Contingent Persatuan Keluarga Polis (Perkep) at the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters here today. Earlier, he witnessed the handover of duties from PDRM Management Department director Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, who was also the Sarawak police commissioner, to his deputy DCP Saifullizan Ishak before Mohamad Zainal begins his duties at Bukit Aman.

items.title: Malaysia’s marine police nab 2,707, record 7,627 cases in national waters this year
items.summary: Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said that the success was the result of continuous enforcement through various operations such as Op Taring Gelora, Op Taring Landai, and inter or intra-agency operations. “The highest offences among them involve the Fisheries Act 1985 with 3,214 cases, the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 (428), the Control of Supplies Control Act 1961 (295), the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the ATIPSOM Act 2007 (213), as well as the Customs Act 1967 (189 cases),” he said at a press conference after officiating the 79th Anniversary celebration of the PPM at the Region One PPM Operations headquarters, Pulau Indah here today. Meanwhile, Mohd Yusri said that PPM as a whole now has 22 projects under the Malaysia Plan (11MP to 13MP) worth RM1.064 billion.

items.title: Malaysia plans A-to-D food grades to nudge manufacturers — and consumers — towards healthier choices
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia could introduce a new food labelling system giving packaged food and drinks nutrition grades from A to D by the end of this year, Health Ministry official Dr Yap Wei Aun has said. Dr Yap, chief executive officer of the Health Ministry’s Health Transformation Office, said prevention was a fundamental aspect of public health and cited the proposed labelling system as an example of the government’s preventive health initiatives. Dr Yap said the Health Ministry had been working with partners, including the food industry, to introduce the “front-of-pack labelling” system, under which bottles of drinks or packaged food would carry an A, B, C or D grade.

items.title: Three separate drug busts net RM3.44m in drugs, five arrests in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Penang police arrested five people, including a couple, and seized various types of drugs worth RM3.44 million in three separate operations between September 21 and 27. Penang Police Chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the raids by the state Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) resulted in the seizure of 8.83 kilogrammes (kg) of heroin, 15.06 kg of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) powder, five litres of liquid MDMA, 182 ecstasy pills and 70 grammes (g) of ketamine. Lim said police seized 3.26 kg of MDMA powder and five litres of liquid MDMA, estimated to be worth RM1.2 million, while investigations found that the couple worked at entertainment centres and obtained the MDMA supply from a drug distribution syndicate.

items.title: F1 fever builds as PM Anwar takes pit-lane walk at Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Formula 1 fever moved up a gear at the Sepang International Circuit today as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined a Pit Lane Walk on the eve of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. This weekend’s race marks Formula 1’s return to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting a world championship round in 2017. Interest has been strong, with nearly 100,000 tickets sold as of Wednesday — a record for races held at the circuit, according to Sepang International Circuit chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Monthly SARA aid credited to recipients’ MyKad from today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Monthly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid has begun being credited to recipients through their respective MyKad cards from today. The Finance Ministry (MoF), in a post on X today, said RM100 in monthly SARA aid would be credited to households receiving Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR), while senior citizens and single individuals would each receive RM50 a month. For recipients of both STR and eKasih, households will receive RM200 in monthly SARA aid, while senior citizens will receive RM150 and single individuals RM100.

items.title: Weather alert: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather was expected to affect several areas in Kedah, namely Kuala Muda, Sik and Baling; Perak, including Hulu Perak, Selama, Kerian, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk; and Kelantan, covering Kuala Krai and Jeli. The same warning was issued for Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Rompin, Maran, Temerloh and Bera in Pahang; and Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Gombak, Petaling, Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, reported Bernama.

items.title: Health Ministry warns against GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after mercury found
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has cancelled the notification of the cosmetic product GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after it was found to contain scheduled poisons, mercury, and is no longer allowed to be sold in the country. Following that, the ministry urged the public to avoid buying and using the involved cosmetics. The statement said that the involved sellers and distributors of the cosmetics must immediately cease the sale and distribution of the cosmetics.

items.title: Indonesia remains a favourite destination for Malaysians as August arrivals jump nearly 29pc
items.summary: JAKARTA, Oct 1 — Malaysians remained Indonesia’s largest source of foreign tourists in August, with arrivals jumping 28.95 per cent year-on-year to 296,227. According to Statistics Indonesia (BPS), Malaysian visitors accounted for 18.52 per cent of the 1.60 million foreign tourist arrivals recorded during the month. BPS said overall foreign tourist arrivals in August rose 6.27 per cent from a year earlier, while arrivals from January to August reached 10.58 million, up 5.38 per cent from the corresponding period in 2025.

items.title: Kuala Terengganu High Court awards RM47,000 to boy who broke leg after being ‘slammed’ onto chair by teacher
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Kuala Terengganu High Court today awarded RM47,000 in damages and costs to a boy, now 13, who suffered a broken right leg in an incident involving a Quran and Fardu Ain (KAFA) teacher four years ago. Judge Yusrin Faidz Yusoff allowed Muhammad Izz Anaqi Mohd Izwan’s appeal and set aside an earlier Sessions Court decision that had dismissed his claim, Utusan Malaysia reported. “The judge failed to assess the evidence of two eyewitnesses and the specialist medical report from Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital.

items.title: Anwar thanks outgoing China ambassador for strengthening ties with Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed his appreciation to outgoing Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia, Ouyang Yujing, for his commitment and contribution towards strengthening cooperation between the two countries. Anwar conveyed his appreciation when he received a farewell call from Ouyang today. He said Malaysia and China had built strong ties across various sectors, including the economy, technology, education and culture.

items.title: Selangor employers who chose Sultan’s Silver Jubilee Oct 25 holiday must observe it, says Labour Dept
items.summary: The department said the special public holiday was declared under subsection 9(1) of the Holidays Act 1951 [Act 369], which allows the state government to declare any day as a public holiday in the state. On September 11, the Selangor state government announced October 26 as a replacement public holiday for the entire state following the declaration of October 25 as a special public holiday in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration. Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the replacement holiday was declared because the celebration and the special public holiday fell on a Sunday.

items.title: Nga Kor Ming offers one month’s ministerial salary for top Housing Ministry innovator
items.summary: He said there is ample scope for innovation at the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) as it oversees housing, local government, cleanliness and solid waste management, fire and rescue services, as well as urban planning, all of which have a direct impact on people’s lives. He said this in his speech at the 2026 Ministry of Housing and Local Government Innovation Day (HIKPKT 2026) here today. HIKPKT 2026, themed “ Memperkasa Inovasi, Memacu Prestasi, Menyejahtera Rakyat ”, showcased 54 innovation projects, including 43 Innovative and Creative Group (KIK) projects and 11 Minister’s Innovation Award (AIM) projects.

items.title: Something next week? Amirudin signals movement in Pakatan-Bersatu talks for Melaka polls
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 1 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) could see a development in its talks with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia as early as next week, its election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today, as the coalition weighs its options ahead of the Melaka state election. Amirudin said PH remained in discussions with various parties and had not ruled out cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN), with all possibilities still on the table. The Selangor menteri besar said PH’s immediate priority in the negotiations was securing electoral success, but stressed that any arrangement would also have to serve the interests of the people.

items.title: RM35 nasi lemak, RM30 Indomie: F1 food prices rev up at Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Formula 1 fans heading to Sepang this weekend might want to leave a little extra room in the budget, with a plate of nasi lemak and fried egg listed at RM35 on an official vendor menu for the race. Four chicken rice meals would come to RM120, while four portions of cut fruit would cost RM80. The prices are listed on a vendor menu circulated through the event’s official QR ordering link .

items.title: Selangor Sultan marks silver jubilee with joyride flight for 149 orphans
items.summary: SUBANG, Oct 1 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and Tengku Permaisuri Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin today treated 149 orphans to a special joyride flight to mark the Sultan’s 25th anniversary on the throne. Their Royal Highnesses, accompanied by Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah, were welcomed at Subang SkyPark by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. Istana Alam Shah, in a statement, said that the Kembara Semenanjung Joyride Flight, involving children from 29 orphanages, officially kicked off the month-long Selangor Sultan Silver Jubilee celebrations in October.

items.title: Malaysia, Singapore eye stronger business links to boost intra-Asean trade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia and Singapore can collaborate to enhance business connectivity within Asean and boost intra-Asean trade by leveraging their strengths in supply chains, the digital economy, and key industries. Miti Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said both countries could explore ways to facilitate greater trade and business linkages among Asean member states, with the long-term objective of increasing the share of intra-Asean trade. The total trade among the 11 countries in Asean is US$4.37 trillion, and among us Asean is only about US$800 billion to US$900 billion.

items.title: US$2m ‘scratch and win’ scam busted in Penang, 29 arrested
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Penang police have busted an international scam syndicate targeting victims, particularly in China and Cambodia, with the arrest of 29 foreign nationals in raids on three bungalows used as call centres in Barat Daya on September 22. The first raid in Teluk Kumbar led to the arrest of 14 Chinese men who had no travel documents, while the second raid in the same area resulted in the detention of three Chinese men, a Cambodian man and three Cambodian women. “The third raid at Solok Bukit Belah, Bayan Baru, saw two Chinese men and six Cambodian women arrested.

items.title: MRT Corp: Overnight lane closures on Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah in George Town until Nov 30 for Mutiara Line works
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Long-term, periodic partial road closures on Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah here will be implemented from today until November 30 to facilitate construction work for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project in the area. In a statement, Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) announced that the closures affecting the stretch from Sungai Nibong Bus Terminal to Batu Uban Road Transport Department (RTD) office will take place between 10pm and 5am to allow for tree cutting and relocation works. “The closures will affect the leftmost lane between Lorong Sungai Dua 1 residential area and Batu Uban RTD office (towards Komtar), as well as the rightmost lane between Lorong Sungai Dua 1 residential area and Batu Uban RTD office in both directions.

items.title: MACC to take six anti-graft proposals before national governance committee
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Six resolutions adopted at the Fifth National Research Conference on Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption (TIAR) 2026 last Friday will be submitted for consideration by the Special Cabinet Committee on National Governance (JKKTN) at its next meeting. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said this was to ensure the resolutions were translated into concrete improvements to the system, particularly efforts to strengthen corruption prevention, rather than remaining merely conference outcomes. Abd Halim said submitting the resolutions to the JKKTN was in line with MACC’s approach of strengthening corruption prevention through a more proactive, targeted and risk-based strategy.

items.title: Penang man charged with secretly filming four women using factory toilet
items.summary: Berita Harian reported that Muhammad Mukhris Sulaiman pleaded not guilty to all five charges and claimed trial after they were read out before Magistrate Sharifah Razali at the Magistrate’s Court in Bukit Mertajam today. For the first four charges, Muhammad Mukhris is accused of filming the women at a factory in Bukit Minyak, in the Central Seberang Perai district, between 11.44am and 6.55pm from September 2 to September 23. Muhammad Mukhris was also charged with possessing several obscene videos during an inspection at the Seberang Perai Tengah district police headquarters compound at 9.30am on September 24.

items.title: Nearly two billion e-invoices submitted by 268,000 taxpayers as of Oct 1, says Inland Revenue Board
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — More than 268,000 taxpayers have submitted 1.99 billion e-invoices as of October 1, the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) said. Its chief executive officer Datuk Abu Tariq Jamaluddin said 196,031 taxpayers accounted for submissions under phase four of the e-invoicing rollout. Abu Tariq said 5,582 taxpayers had submitted e-invoices under phase one, followed by 14,579 under phase two and 51,815 under phase three.

items.title: Education Ministry halts school programmes involving freelance speakers amid allegations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek has ordered the immediate suspension of all programmes involving freelance speakers in schools following allegations circulating on social media involving a freelance speaker who had previously conducted programmes with pupils. Fadhlina said she was aware of several allegations involving the speaker and had instructed the Education Ministry to obtain further information on the matter. Her statement came after allegations involving the freelance speaker and school pupils circulated on social media.

items.title: ‘If the price is me, I’ll pay it’: Border agency chief Shuhaily ready to face action over viral KLIA incident
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said he was prepared to accept any action taken by the government over a viral video from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), saying he would take responsibility for what happened. Therefore, whatever decision they make, I will accept it,” he said, according to Utusan Malaysia . Shuhaily said two unidentified individuals then appeared and began filming while officers were interviewing the foreign national.

items.title: ICJ? Asean? Civil suits? What can Malaysia, others do about Indonesia’s choking haze?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Haze from Indonesian wildfires has blanketed neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore for more than a month, closing schools and sending respiratory complaints skyrocketing. It is not the first time Indonesian haze has caused a regional pollution crisis, but neighbouring countries have few options for legal recourse, experts say: Case at the ICJ Suggestions that Malaysia and Singapore take Indonesia to the UN’s highest judicial organ, the International Court of Justice in The Hague, face a basic obstacle: “The main issue is jurisdiction, as the ICJ generally requires the consent of both states,” said Professor Mohd Hazmi Mohd Rusli of Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia. Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore are neither signatories nor parties to the 1979 Convention on Long-range Transboundary Air Pollution, a European-centred treaty framework intended to curb cross-border air pollution.
